issue.standard_remedy: Consolidate tail suppliers into preferred suppliers
issue.summary: 27 of 70 suppliers share the last 20% of category spend

plan.diagnosis: The Professional services category exhibits severe fragmentation with an HHI of 187 (well below the 1,500 threshold for healthy concentration) across 70 suppliers and $13,383,015 in spend. 27 tail suppliers collectively account for $2,672,106 (20% of category spend), indicating poor leverage, duplicative overhead, and process inefficiency; even the top supplier (Quartz Allied Packaging Inc.) holds only 4% share, demonstrating lack of strategic partnerships.

remedy_steps.step: Conduct RFI with top 10 suppliers by spend to assess capability breadth, capacity for expanded scope, and willingness to offer volume discounts for consolidation of the $2,672,106 tail spend
Issue competitive RFP to 3-5 qualified strategic partners with bundled SOW covering services currently provided by tail suppliers, targeting 12-18% savings on consolidated tail spend
Award master service agreements (MSAs) to 2-3 preferred suppliers, negotiate tiered pricing based on annual volume commitments, and establish governance model with quarterly business reviews
Implement transition plan to migrate active projects from tail suppliers to preferred partners, with 90-day wind-down for non-critical suppliers
Establish purchase requisition approval workflows requiring pre-approval for any Professional services spend outside preferred supplier panel

plan.expected_impact: Consolidating the $2,672,106 tail spend into 2-3 strategic suppliers is expected to deliver $320,653 to $480,979 in annual savings through volume leverage (12-18%) plus reduction in transaction costs and supplier management overhead.
kpis: Reduce Professional services supplier count from 70 to <15 within 6 months
Increase category HHI from 187 to >800 within 12 months
Achieve top 3 suppliers representing >60% of category spend
Realize $400,000+ in savings from tail spend consolidation
Reduce average PO cycle time for Professional services by 30%
risks: Service quality degradation if preferred suppliers lack niche expertise currently provided by tail suppliers
Stakeholder resistance from business units with established relationships with incumbent tail suppliers
Transition disruption to active projects during supplier wind-down period
Preferred suppliers may lack capacity to absorb $2.67M in additional volume within 6-month timeframe
Multi-ERP environment (SAP, Oracle EBS, Dynamics 365, NetSuite, Coupa) creates complexity in enforcing preferred supplier controls consistently across all systems
erp_actions: SAP: Create source list entries (ME01) for 2-3 preferred Professional services suppliers with exclusive flags; apply LFA1/LFB1 posting blocks to 27 tail suppliers after transition
Oracle EBS: Update approved supplier list (ASL) for Professional services category, set preferred supplier flags, and configure sourcing rules to route requisitions to strategic partners
Dynamics 365: Deactivate vendor records for tail suppliers post-transition; configure procurement policies to restrict PO creation outside preferred supplier list
NetSuite: Update vendor category assignments, set preferred vendor status for strategic partners, implement saved searches to flag non-compliant requisitions

Coupa: Configure catalog punch-outs and preferred forms for 2-3 strategic suppliers; set up approval routing rules requiring VP-level sign-off for non-preferred Professional services purchases >$5,000
Cross-ERP: Implement master data governance process to maintain synchronized preferred supplier lists and blocking status across all five systems within 48 hours of any change
